title: T1048.001 — Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol - Exfiltration Over Symmetric Encrypted Non-C2 Protocol
subtitle: Watch the whole attack in eight steps, then read the same story in text.
aria: T1048.001 - Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol - Exfiltration Over Symmetric Encrypted Non-C2 Protocol

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.tip: Sensitive data - What is at risk

steps.title: Foothold
steps.caption: A phishing attachment runs on the workstation and hands control to the attacker. Office starts a hidden script process to do the work. The SOC sees one suspicious Office child process in EDR, but the score stays low because nothing else has happened yet
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Stage and encrypt
steps.caption: The malware gathers research files into one archive and encrypts it with a symmetric cipher such as AES. The shared key sits inside the malware configuration. An archive-like file with high entropy (data that looks random) appears in a temp folder; the SOC sees no alert at this point because file writes alone look normal
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Open channel
steps.caption: The malware opens a raw TCP connection to a rented virtual private server (VPS) on port 8443. The firewall records a new flow to a bare IP on a port with no known service. The SOC has not been alerted, but first-seen logs now hold the pair of host and port
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Stream out
steps.caption: The encrypted archive leaves in steady chunks - about 180 MB in total. The connection shows large bytes out, yet the TLS parser finds nothing to decode. To the SOC this means one thing: the flow is encrypted, but it is not TLS
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Decrypt at VPS
steps.caption: The attacker side holds the same shared key and rebuilds the archive from the arriving chunks. The stolen files are now outside the company in readable form. From the inside, the stream still looks like a quiet file transfer
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: SOC review
steps.caption: The daily baseline for bytes out per port gets a new high-water mark on 8443. A volume alert fires because a port with no known service owner crossed the line. The analyst opens a case and pulls the flow records
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.caption: The analyst joins the network story with the endpoint story. EDR lineage (the process family tree) shows the same process wrote the .bin file and then opened the socket. Staging plus egress in one process is a strong sign of exfiltration
